name: Fosgonimeton

lead: Fosgonimeton is an investigational drug from Athira Pharma that was tested for Alzheimer's disease. It is described as a prodrug of dihexa that boosts HGF/MET signaling.
It has no studied role in appearance. It is a related name in research-compound discussions.

paras: It is described as a positive modulator of the HGF/MET neurotrophic pathway, reported in preclinical studies to promote neuronal health and cognition-related effects.
It is not approved for any use. A phase I trial reported on safety and tolerability in volunteers and Alzheimer's patients; details of later-phase results are in the primary literature.

ATH-1017 for Treatment of Mild to Moderate Alzheimer's Disease

lead: Fosgonimeton (also ATH-1017 or NDX-1017) is an investigational small molecule developed by Athira Pharma as a prodrug of an active metabolite, dihexa, that enhances signaling of hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) at its MET receptor. [1][2] It was studied as a possible treatment for Alzheimer's disease and other dementias rather than for any cosmetic purpose.
In looksmaxxing and longevity-oriented communities it appears mainly as a related name to the research peptide-like compound dihexa. It is not an approved medicine anywhere.
Published human data consist of a phase I trial in healthy volunteers and people with Alzheimer's disease and a registered phase 2/3 trial; the rest of the literature is preclinical. [3][4][5]

paras: Preclinical work describes fosgonimeton as a positive modulator of the HGF/MET neurotrophic system, reported to promote neurotrophic and procognitive effects in cell and animal models of dementia. [2] Later laboratory papers reported that it reduced amyloid-beta toxicity in neuron cultures and models of Alzheimer's disease. [6][7]

A randomized, placebo-controlled phase I trial (NCT03298672) evaluated safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in healthy volunteers and people with Alzheimer's disease. [3] A phase 2/3 trial in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease (NCT04488419) is registered as completed with 554 participants. [4] A phase I absorption, metabolism and excretion study used radiolabeled drug in 8 healthy volunteers. [5] A 2025 paper reports on the drug in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease. [8] No studies have examined it for appearance outcomes.
Fosgonimeton is not sold as a consumer product. Review articles on emerging treatments for Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia list it among investigational agents. [9]
